---
title: 'Employee address migration suppliers'
description: 'Inactive stable identity SQL, Auth and Web suppliers and their qualification boundaries.'
---

The portable protocol and suppliers live in
`packages/utils/src/internal-accounts/employee-address-migration*.ts`.
Infrastructure retains compatible re-exports. The Web handler is a factory only;
there is no installed route, runtime environment switch or UI consumer. Default
availability remains off. Supplier tests do not authorize account execution.

## Address and identity policy

The operation changes a canonical lowercase managed-subdomain address
to the same localpart at exactly `tuturuuu.com`. It rejects external domains,
root-address sources, a changed localpart, self-action, unknown ownership,
conflicting reservations, stale revisions and unverified source identities.
It never requests another Auth UUID, account creation/deletion, password,
metadata, administrator grants, ban changes or an email-confirmation override.
The provider port exposes only a read and an email update on the original UUID.

A protected journal supplier must reauthorize the confirmed active root
administrator and lock/revalidate the original actor, UUID, both addresses and
all competing CREATE/RESTORE/migration reservations in every transaction. The
supplier must independently observe real Auth/provider identity IDs, the public
identity, workspace memberships, grants, saved data and mailbox routes. A caller
supplied boolean or fingerprint is not administrator or preservation proof.
Fingerprints must use documented canonical snapshots and must exclude only the
specific email fields that this operation is allowed to change.

## Persisted operation protocol

An original operation UUID binds the actor, target UUID, source/destination,
revision, immutable-state fingerprint and provider-identity fingerprint.
Reservation must be durably idempotent on that whole binding, with unique
unresolved target/address ownership. An atomic attempt claim returns true to
exactly one invocation; every replay returns false. Neither lease expiry nor
process restart may reissue that claim. Attempt IDs are server-generated UUIDs.

The executor requires an independent committed read after reservation, attempt
claim and completion. A claimed attempt also needs its one-time acknowledgement;
a persisted attempted row alone cannot authorize another provider request.
Crashes and lost responses retain the original operation for inspection. Even a
reserved replay is inspection-only. No expiry, replacement operation, rollback,
compensation or automatic provider retry is part of this contract.

A provider email update must use the supported admin update on the original UUID
with `{ email }` only. It must perform one request without transport retry and
preserve existing provider identity IDs. Actual GoTrue behavior, verification
challenges, secure-email-change settings and concurrent external administrators
must be qualified before installing that supplier. An unverified destination or
changed identity remains pending; the protocol never sets `email_confirm`.

Inspection can complete a named attempted operation after observing the verified
destination and unchanged identity. Completion must independently verify actual
Auth state and preservation, then atomically update only approved registry/public
email projections and mailbox routing with a revision increment. The final
readback must match the original binding, completed phase and exact next revision.
A completed replay returns that original receipt without another provider write.

## Evidence and remaining gates

`employee-address-migration.test.ts` exercises the real source executor with an
explicitly in-memory journal/provider fixture. It covers concurrent callers,
strict old/new tuples, lost reserve/claim/provider acknowledgements, false
acknowledgements, source/destination verification, identity drift, immutable-state
drift, completed replay and inspection without relaunch.

This fixture does **not** establish durable persistence, SQL lock/ACL behavior,
real email change/verification, mailbox delivery, public profile convergence or
UUID/membership/data preservation in a real project. Those remain supplier gates.
The additive `20261017010000_employee_address_migrations.sql` supplier implements
service-only journal transactions with direct table access revoked, durable
unique target/address reservations and a one-time claim. Its scope is deliberately
legacy accounts absent from CREATE/RESTORE registries with email-provider-only
identities, first revision zero to one.
It requires existing active source and destination mailboxes and matching active
domains, with both mailboxes owned exclusively by the target UUID. It does not
provision mail, change addresses on mailboxes, set onboarding metadata or convert
the account into the CREATE registry. The retained completed migration is its
address registry; the existing Auth synchronization trigger owns the public email
projection. A missing route or registry conflict fails closed.

The immutable snapshot covers Auth password/metadata/ban/role/phone state, the
public profile, private details except email projections, workspace memberships,
workspace role assignments/definitions/permissions, platform grants, owned
mailboxes, mailbox memberships and the two domains. It hashes these protected
values without returning the snapshot. Saved application rows remain linked to
the unchanged UUID; this is not an exhaustive snapshot of every application table.
Migration transactions first try exclusive global address admission without
waiting. Busy admission raises SQLSTATE `55P03` before any capability or state
change; it must not queue behind a shared writer and block later shared writers.
Guarded ordinary writers take shared admission before statement row locks. This avoids
the destination-row/advisory inversion without serializing ordinary writers with
each other. Both original and destination addresses remain reserved permanently.
Both RPCs and guarded writers require READ COMMITTED isolation. The RPC uses
NOWAIT for row and authorization-table locks after admission; contention aborts
without issuing a claim, releasing admission for existing CREATE/RESTORE/provider
transactions that already hold rows. There is no automatic retry. Authorization dependencies use
short transaction SHARE locks to fence concurrent
permission revocation and absent-row grant changes. Qualification must measure
that lock scope before activation. Reservation triggers also fence Auth users and
identities, public email profiles, mailboxes, reserved grants and CREATE intents.

The identity fingerprint is lowercase SHA-256 of compact UTF-8 JSON tuples
`[[identity_id, provider, user_id], ...]`, sorted by canonical UUID `identity_id`.
GoTrue JSON `identity_id` maps to SQL `auth.identities.id`; JSON `id` is the
provider-specific ID. SQL explicitly constructs compact JSON under C collation.
Email fields are excluded so the original identity remains recognizable.

The provider uses the installed supported `auth.admin.updateUserById(id, {email})`
contract. Its independent verification requires the matching email identity's
`email_verified=true`, the confirmed timestamp, no pending email and an active
account. Upstream GoTrue's admin email-only path can set identity verification
false while retaining the confirmed timestamp. That observation stays pending;
there is no confirmation override or automatic retry. See the
[GoTrue admin handler](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/v2.197.0/internal/api/admin.go#L235-L284)
and [supported JavaScript API](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-admin-updateuserbyid).

The disposable SQL qualification runner exercises the actual migration on an
isolated PostgreSQL fixture with explicitly reduced prerequisite tables. It is
not a full migration-history replay or a real GoTrue provider result. It includes
a three-session blocking-exclusive control and all four RPC actions under shared
contention, checking `55P03`, unrelated Auth-writer progress and unchanged fixture
state. Competing claims are drained without retry; exactly one successful
capability must match the durable journal attempt and independent inspection.
The loser may return false or the exact owned SQLSTATE `55P03` admission-busy
envelope; other errors fail qualification. The 10-assertion composed SQL packet
does not run these concurrency cases.
Run it only with separate admission for its disposable database lifecycle, via
the canonical resource queue:

```sh
ttr resources run -- node apps/database/scripts/employee-address-migration-qualification.mjs
```

The runner retains the exact observed daemon identity
`docker-desktop linux 29.8.2` as a pre-creation admission fence. This identifies
the originally targeted local fixture; it is not a PostgreSQL compatibility
requirement or approval for another daemon/version. A mismatch requires a
separately reviewed target/admission decision, not removal of the check.

A separate real-provider runner uses cached GoTrue `v2.197.0` and PostgreSQL
`17.11.0.004` images on an internal Docker network without published ports.
GoTrue distinguishes user confirmation from identity verification:
[admin creation](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/v2.197.0/internal/api/admin.go#L473-L528)
creates the email identity with the default false verification claim, then
[confirms the user](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/v2.197.0/internal/models/user.go#L488-L507).
Magic-link OTP uses recovery verification, which does not update that identity
flag. The installed SDK forwards these fields; it does not repair the mismatch.
The Utils transport regression owns an SDK devDependency at the existing locked
version. Its strict isolated dependency layout must resolve that import directly;
a hoisted root SDK can mask a missing package declaration during local checks.
A confirmed timestamp plus correlated email alone therefore does not satisfy this
migration's stricter verification contract. The guard remains unchanged.

The positive fixture creates an unconfirmed disposable source and uses supported
`generateLink({type: 'signup', ...})` followed by signup `verifyOtp`.
[Signup verification](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/v2.197.0/internal/api/verify.go#L294-L375)
sets the matching identity flag through GoTrue. This fixture path is not a repair
procedure for already-confirmed legacy accounts; generating a signup link for
an already-confirmed user is rejected by the pinned server.

The real supplier then issues one email-only PUT on that UUID. The runner drops
the successful response to exercise an unknown acknowledgement, reads back the
actual destination, and proves protocol replay and a repeated supplier call do
not issue another PUT. UUID, identity IDs, password hash, metadata, ban state,
confirmation timestamp, sessions and refresh-token rows are compared privately.
A separate fixture-owned mail table is also compared; that table does not prove
preservation of the full product mail schema or hosted delivery. The journal is
an explicit fixture. The destination identity becomes unverified, so the result
remains `pending` for inspection; this is positive provider mutation and
preservation qualification, not a completed address migration.

```sh
ttr resources run -- bun apps/database/scripts/employee-address-migration-gotrue-qualification.ts --source=signup
```

The retained negative mode creates the source with admin confirmation and uses
magic-link OTP. It must remain unverified under the stricter contract, refuse the
supplier change with zero PUTs, and preserve its original snapshot:

```sh
ttr resources run -- bun apps/database/scripts/employee-address-migration-gotrue-qualification.ts --source=magiclink
```

The full-schema workflow's separate `include_address_migration=true` selection
adds `employee-address-migration.sql` with exactly 10 rollback assertions. It
qualifies the legacy SQL path and existing profile trigger, without treating SQL
simulation as real GoTrue verification. Foundation and journal receipts remain
incompatible and keep their original defaults; see the
[qualification profiles](./employee-schema-qualification).

Before runtime binding, apply the full schema in the approved isolated fixture,
verify generated types, real GoTrue and Web transport behavior, hosted mail routing,
and the exact Web/Infrastructure builds in CI. Existing schema CI guards remain
in force; a reduced fixture never replaces that gate. Record a scoped
activation/rollback plan separately. CREATE or RESTORE receipts do not qualify
this migration, and production/provider/SQL actions require separate authority.
